data.text:
🇦🇺 AUSTRALIAN ACTIVIST CLAIMS POLICE DEMANDED HE DELETE POST LINKING JOURNALIST TO ISIS PROPAGANDA

Drew Pavlou says Queensland Police called him December 28, demanding he remove a December 23 X post accusing journalist Craig Hill of "promoting ISIS propaganda" by linking the Bondi Beach terror attack to "anti-Zionist motives."

Context: the December 14 attack killed 15 people at a Hanukkah celebration. Authorities confirmed it was ISIS-inspired - 2 homemade ISIS flags found in the shooter's car, attackers traveled to Philippines beforehand, surviving shooter charged with 59 offenses including terrorism.

The shooter, Naveed Akram, worshipped at radical preacher Wissam Haddad's Al Madina Dawah Centre in Bankstown. 

Haddad was found to have violated Australia's racial hatred laws in 2025. Pavlou had warned about Haddad two years ago.

Pavlou's claim: police called it "intimidation and proof of uneven enforcement," especially after authorities ignored earlier threats from ISIS preacher Haddad. 

Pavlou's track record: suspended from University of Queensland, arrested multiple times for anti-CCP protests, detained 23 hours in London over fabricated bomb threat, ejected from Australian Parliament for being a "known activist," fined $10,000 for holding protest signs.

The pattern: activist criticizes radical preacher whose follower commits ISIS terror attack, then gets police call asking him to delete the criticism.

Source: @DrewPavlou
